questions.q: Values 10, 12, 11, 13, 40. Which statistic is least affected by the 40?
Which window do you use to score x(t) without leakage?
Mean 50, standard deviation 5, value 62. What is the z-score?
Scenario: a sensor series has a steady upward trend. A global z-score flags the last 10% of points as anomalies. What is the best fix?
options: Use a rolling window (or remove the trend first)
Delete the last 10% of the data
why: This hides real anomalies and the idea is still wrong.
Correct: the rolling mean follows the trend, so normal growth is not flagged.
You would lose real data and the problem returns.

questions.q: Scenario: your rolling window contains a past spike, and later spikes are missed. What helps most?
why: Correct: median and MAD ignore a few extreme values.
Length does not remove the effect of the spike on std.

questions.q: Which are good practices for a rolling z-score? (select all)
options: Shift the window by one step
Include the current point in the window
Choose a window that matches the pattern length
why: Yes: for example 7 for weekly data.
